## What is in a file

```{=html}
<div class="store-tree">nba/2025-26/
├── player-logs/   <span class="hl">nba_2025-26_player-logs.csv</span>         one row per player per game played
├── team-logs/     <span class="hl">nba_2025-26_team-logs.csv</span>           one row per team per game
├── play-by-play/  <span class="hl">nba_2025-26_play-by-play.csv.zip</span>    one row per event
├── schedule/      <span class="hl">nba_2025-26_schedule.csv</span>            one row per game played
└── first-events/  <span class="hl">nba_2025-26_first-events.csv</span>        one row per game</div>
```

- **Plain CSV** with a header row. It opens in Excel, Sheets, R, pandas or DuckDB with no cleanup step.
- **One schema per dataset.** The oldest season has the same columns as the newest, so seasons stack.
- **IDs that join.** Game, team and player IDs are the same strings in every file for a league.
- **A dictionary for every column**, on the dataset's page and in a README beside the file.
- **Free samples.** Every dataset page shows real rows and links a sample CSV.

## The file nobody else sells

Who won the opening tip, who scored first and with what kind of shot, each team's first scorer, and the first rebound, assist, steal, block and three of every game: one row per game, back more than a decade. We have been labeling the first minute of basketball games from play-by-play for years, because our own models run on it. Now it is a file: [NBA](nba-first-events.qmd) and [WNBA](wnba-first-events.qmd).

## How buying works

1. Add seasons to the cart and pay once by card. No account, no subscription.
2. Your library link opens the moment the payment clears. Every file you own is listed there.
3. Completed seasons are final. A season pass is rebuilt every morning until the season ends, then it is yours to keep.

More on formats, delivery and the license in [how the store works](help.qmd).

## Why these files hold up

We are a team of data scientists who run prediction models on this data every day of every season. A wrong row costs us before it costs you, so the pipeline that builds these files is the one we depend on ourselves: pulled from source every morning, checked against box score totals, and rebuilt when a league issues a stat correction.

## Coming next

Two things we already hold and are packaging for the store: **odds history** (the price at every sportsbook, every 30 minutes, for the markets we model) and **our projections** (a probability for every player and game). If you want either sooner, or a custom pull, [tell us](../contact.qmd).

::: {.faq-item}
### What format are the files in?

Plain CSV, UTF-8, with a header row. Play-by-play is one CSV inside a standard .zip because of its size. Nothing needs an account, an API key or special software.
:::

::: {.faq-item}
### Is any of the data free?

Every dataset has a free sample you can download from its page. The [stats pages](../stats/index.qmd) also publish first basket history for every NBA and WNBA team and first-inning records for every MLB team, free to read.
:::

::: {.faq-item}
### Can I use the data in my own work?

Yes. Analyze it, build on it and publish what you make from it. The one thing the [license](help.qmd#license) rules out is passing along or reselling the files themselves.
:::

::: {.faq-item}
### Do you sell your picks here?

No. The store is data only. The picks are a separate [subscription](../subscribe.qmd).
:::
